properties.name: Hector Pieterson Memorial & Museum
properties.summary: Commemorates the schoolchildren killed by police during the 16 June 1976 Soweto uprising, named for the first student shot on the day.

properties.name: Regina Mundi Church
properties.summary: Soweto's largest Catholic church, used as a refuge and meeting place during police crackdowns on anti-apartheid gatherings through the 1970s and 1980s.

properties.name: Walter Sisulu Square of Dedication
properties.summary: Site of the Congress of the People in Kliptown, where the Freedom Charter was adopted on 26 June 1955.

properties.name: Constitution Hill
properties.summary: Former prison complex that held Mahatma Gandhi, Nelson Mandela, and Winnie Madikizela-Mandela among many others; now the seat of South Africa's Constitutional Court.

properties.name: Liliesleaf Farm
properties.summary: Underground headquarters of the ANC and Umkhonto we Sizwe in the early 1960s; the July 1963 police raid here led directly to the Rivonia Trial.

properties.name: Apartheid Museum
properties.summary: Museum tracing the rise and fall of apartheid through the twentieth century, opened in 2001 south of central Johannesburg.

properties.name: Freedom Park
properties.summary: National heritage precinct and memorial in Pretoria honouring those who died in South Africa's conflicts, including the struggle against apartheid.

properties.name: Sharpeville Human Rights Precinct
properties.summary: Memorial and precinct marking the 21 March 1960 Sharpeville massacre, where police killed 69 people at a protest against pass laws; the site of South Africa's 1996 constitutional signing.
